spec.wording: This is a synthetic-world calibration only. It does not prove that any real strategy works. It checks the false-positive rate and power of the frozen test procedure. No strategy is approved by it; it only licenses or blocks inference.
spec.replaces: an informal text draft that used accuracy-style limits (FPR <= 0.05) and a 2%-per-day effect size; neither matched the frozen money statistic
spec.tested_quantity: for each of the four hypotheses (ema50_200, breakout20, weekly_mom_b1, meanrev_short_b1): mean daily active return, defined in batch1 spec as strategy net return minus E_t x benchmark return, over the evaluable days
spec.procedure_under_test: the exact real-run procedure: build daily bars, run the strategy engine with its warm-up and turnover, compute the daily active-return series, resample blocks of days, take the one-sided lower bound at 1 - alpha_individual

alpha.note: false positive = lower bound above 0 in a world with no skill

synthetic_world.panel: N coins (as in the frozen universe) by T days (the real evaluable window length), starting on the real first dates and with the real missing-day pattern (invalid coin-days are invalid in the worlds too)
synthetic_world.returns: daily log return of coin i = beta_i x F_t + e_it; F_t = common factor with stochastic volatility; e_it with coin-specific stochastic volatility; innovations Student t(4) scaled to unit variance; zero predictability by construction (no autocorrelation, no cross-sectional or time-series signal)
synthetic_world.volatility: log volatility follows AR(1) with the half-life of the world type and stationary sd 0.25 (common) and 0.30 (coin); shock sd = stationary sd x sqrt(1-phi^2); common factor sd 2.0%/day times exp(log vol); coin sd 2.5%/day times exp(coin log vol); stationary start
synthetic_world.drift: zero in the base null; one added world type carries drift so that buy-and-hold earns about +60% a year, to show the exposure-matched benchmark removes it
synthetic_world.limit_of_the_generator: volatility persists but returns have no persistent mean regimes; real markets have multi-month trends that give trend rules a real edge or a real drag. This calibration tests the bootstrap's error rate, not realism.
synthetic_world.model_selfcheck: before any calibration, for every world type: simulated daily-return autocorrelation at lags 1 and 30 within 0.03 of zero; simulated volatility persistence (autocorrelation of absolute returns at lag 30) within 0.05 of its theoretical value computed from the AR(1) parameters; mean of F_t within 4 standard errors of its target; a planted +0.05% daily active return recovered within 10% by the engine. Any failure stops everything and nothing is loosened. [v2: tolerances unchanged; theoretical lag-30 abs-return autocorrelation recomputed with stationary variance 0.0625 (common) and 0.09 (coin); any failure stops everything, no v3 on the same ground, batch stays descriptive and forward-only]

gross_null.rule: the null worlds are evaluated gross of costs: the statistic is the mean daily active return before transaction costs
gross_null.reason: costs are a deterministic drag known in advance; including them would make the null mean negative and hide false positives. The real run reports and tests net returns.
gross_null.consequence: calibration says nothing about whether costs destroy an edge; the real run's cost handling needs its own engine self-checks

spec.limits_rule: limits keep the stage-1 rates (11 of 986 per seed, 18 of 1,972 pooled), rounded down; chosen so a correct test at nominal 0.5% is wrongly rejected about 1% of the time
spec.judged_cells: each hypothesis x world type x block length is one cell; a block length qualifies only if every cell passes both the per-seed and pooled limits

precision_rule.text: if a cell that passes the count limits has a pooled 95% Clopper-Pearson upper bound above 2%, that world type expands to the next stage with the same seeds, earlier worlds reused; if still flagged at the last stage the status is NEEDS MORE WORLDS: no block selected, no power run, nothing real read

spec.selection: the shortest block length that qualifies in every cell; if none qualifies the status is NO BLOCK QUALIFIES and the real batch is descriptive and forward-only

power.how: add the planted amount to every evaluable day of the strategy's active return in a type-A and type-B world; use seed 1 for the planted-world sweep
power.target: 80% detection of the one-sided lower bound above 0, per hypothesis
power.report: the smallest planted effect reaching 80% is that hypothesis's minimum detectable effect; the real run states it next to the result
power.if_none_reaches_80: that hypothesis is descriptive only, even if the bootstrap is calibrated

effects_on_inference.calibration_passes_and_power_ok: inference allowed for hypotheses with MDE reported
effects_on_inference.calibration_passes_but_power_fails: inference allowed in form only; a null means 'no effect larger than MDE'
effects_on_inference.calibration_fails: descriptive and forward-only; wording: 'The calibration did not license inference.'

spec.stop_rules: a failed model self-check, NO BLOCK QUALIFIES or NEEDS MORE WORLDS stops the batch; limits, block lengths, world types and parameters are never changed afterwards; a changed design is a new version with a new hash
spec.isolation: the calibration code reads no database and no real return, and writes only a result file
outputs: batch1_calib_result_v3.json (counts per cell, selection, MDE per hypothesis, status, engine hash, clipped coin-day count, per-type max daily return)
order: write the engine and calibration code with its own synthetic self-checks
not_decided: whether batch-wide alpha 0.0025 replaces per-family 0.005 (this addendum uses 0.005)
runtime: re-timed by quick mode on v2 worlds before any full run
spec.v1_status: STOPPED: quick mode failed 3 model self-checks (B coin lag1 -0.081, B coin abs lag30 0.257 vs 0.149, D factor lag1 -0.071); worlds B and D numerically absurd (daily returns up to 1e16+). No calibration result, no real data read.
spec.the_one_change: each coin daily log return in every synthetic world is clipped to [-ln2, +ln2] (about -50% / +100% simple), applied after beta x F + e + drift and after the pre-start days are zeroed; the number of clipped coin-days is counted and reported. Justified by synthetic numerics only; no real-data or strategy result used; not tuned to make any strategy pass. Everything else is unchanged from v2.
spec.numerical_guard: the run stops with WORLD INVALID only if a world is non-finite; clipped coin-days are counted and reported per run; the +1000% rule of v2 is removed because the clip makes it unreachable
spec.drift_note: drift added equally to every coin daily log return (ln1.6/365), not scaled by beta; mean gross active return per cell reported as a diagnostic
spec.v2_status: STOPPED: full run hit its own WORLD INVALID guard at type A, seed 1, world 651 (max daily simple return 222.67 vs +1000% guard); 650 worlds done; false-positive counts deliberately not read; no real data or strategy result used.
spec.model_selfcheck_note: self-checks test the unclipped factor and coin components with unchanged tolerances; any failure stops everything; no v4 on the same ground, batch stays descriptive and forward-only
